extracted.intended_audience: general readers, genre writers, and potential contributors interested in Apex Magazine
extracted.subtask_short: submitting short fiction to Apex Magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writers and potential contributors about the kinds of work Apex Magazine publishes (genre, formats, publication cadence, and reputation). Useful for authors targeting Apex with short fiction, reviews, or interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre focus — horror and science fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Apex Magazine is an American horror and science fiction magazine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should fit within the magazine's primary genres of horror and science fiction; the magazine positions itself in speculative fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted content types — short fiction, reviews, interviews (poetry discontinued)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subscription webzine, Apex Magazine, contains short fiction, reviews, and interviews. It also published poems until 2017.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary content to target is short fiction; the magazine also runs reviews and interviews. Note that poetry was discontinued in 2017, so poets should verify current policy on the submissions page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication cadence and medium — bimonthly, digital-only since 2020
rubrics_metrics.description: After an 8-month hiatus starting in 2019, the magazine returned on January 5, 2020, with issue 121 and transitioned to a bimonthly publication cycle. Upon return from its 2019 hiatus, Apex resumed digital-only publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a bimonthly schedule and digital publication; timing of acceptance and publication will follow that cadence. Historically they used print-on-demand for print runs, but current issues are digital-only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader engagement — Story of the Year voted by readers
rubrics_metrics.description: The magazine promotes a Story of the Year which is voted on by readers and fans of the magazine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories published in Apex may be eligible for reader-driven recognition; building audience engagement can influence post-publication visibility (e.g., Story of the Year voting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial leadership and taste — award-winning editors
rubrics_metrics.description: The monthly magazine was edited by award-winning author Catherynne M. Valente from issues #15–29, Hugo Award-winning editor Lynne M. Thomas from issues #30–55, and Sigrid Ellis from issues #56–67. The current editor-in-chief is Lesley Conner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial changes and the presence of established, award-winning editors signal particular tastes and professional editorial standards; prospective contributors should review recent issues to gauge current editorial preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation and awards — nominations and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been nominated for several awards including the Hugo Award. Fiction published in Apex has been nominated for the Nebula Award. Poetry published in Apex has been nominated for the Rhysling Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apex has a track record of publishing award-recognized work; aiming for high craft and originality aligns with the magazine's published output and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated publishing opportunities — Apex Publications (anthologies, novels, nonfiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apex Publications has released a number of novels, nonfiction books and anthologies, including short story collections and themed anthologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should be aware that Apex also operates a publishing arm that produces anthologies and books; strong or themed pieces might have additional opportunities beyond the magazine itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find submission details — 'Submissions' page link
rubrics_metrics.description: The article references a 'Submissions' page on apex-magazine.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For concrete submission rules (word counts, simultaneous submissions, rights, formatting), consult the magazine's official Submissions page; the Wikipedia article does not reproduce those technical requirements.
